resumen: Verbs and formulas for summarising someone else's text accurately (the author argues, claims, acknowledges…) and paraphrasing techniques to avoid copying word for word. Key for the summary task and for presenting an article.

explicacion.texto: The reporting verb conveys the author's attitude and yours: “states” is neutral; “claims” suggests that it has not been proven; “acknowledges” indicates that the author admits something against their own thesis. Choosing the right verb is part of the summary.

filas: argue (that)
to put forward reasons for a view (es: sostener, argumentar)
The author argues that taxes should rise.
claim (that)
to say something is true without clear proof (es: afirmar sin pruebas claras)
He claims that the policy has worked.
state / point out
to say / to draw attention to (es: afirmar / señalar)
She points out that the data is old.
contend / maintain
to argue firmly (es: sostener con firmeza)
Critics maintain that it is unfair.
acknowledge / concede
to admit (es: reconocer, admitir)
The writer acknowledges some risks.
suggest
to propose or imply (es: sugerir, dar a entender)
The study suggests a link.
stress / emphasise / highlight
to give special importance to (es: subrayar, destacar)
The report highlights the role of education.
warn (that / of / against)
to tell someone about a danger (es: advertir)
Experts warn of a new recession.
question / challenge
to express doubt about (es: poner en duda, cuestionar)
She questions the official figures.
dismiss / reject
to refuse to accept or consider (es: descartar, rechazar)
He dismisses the idea as naive.
call for / advocate
to demand publicly / to support (es: reclamar, abogar por)
The article calls for stricter rules.
conclude (that)
to reach a final judgement (es: concluir)
The authors conclude that more research is needed.
outline / describe
to give the main points / to describe (es: esbozar, describir)
The first section outlines the problem.
examine / explore
to look at in detail (es: analizar, explorar)
The book explores the roots of populism.
attribute X to Y
to say that X is caused by Y (es: atribuir X a Y)
He attributes the crisis to poor regulation.
The text deals with…
the text is about… (es: el texto trata de…)
The text deals with migration.
The main point is that…
the central idea is that… (es: la idea principal es que…)
The main point is that cities must adapt.
According to the author,…
as the author says,… (es: según el autor,…)
According to the author, the euro is stronger than ever.
In the author's view,…
in the author's opinion,… (es: en opinión del autor,…)
In the author's view, the reform came too late.
In short / In a nutshell
briefly / in very few words (es: en resumen, en pocas palabras)
In a nutshell, the plan failed.
to put it differently
in other words (es: dicho de otra manera)
To put it differently, demand is too weak.

items: Paraphrasing techniques: change the word class (decide → decision), use synonyms, change active to passive and reorder the information.
Grammar: “suggest” does not take “to” + infinitive: “suggest that we wait” or “suggest waiting”.
“Resume” does not mean “resumir”: the word is “summarise” (British) or “summarize” (American).

ejemplos.frase: The author argues that rural areas have been forgotten by politicians.
ejemplos.traduccion: El autor sostiene que los políticos se han olvidado de las zonas rurales.

ejemplos.frase: She acknowledges that her proposal would be expensive.
ejemplos.traduccion: Reconoce que su propuesta saldría cara.

ejemplos.frase: The article calls for a ban on mobile phones in schools.
ejemplos.traduccion: El artículo reclama prohibir los móviles en los colegios.

ejemplos.frase: Scientists warn that the glacier could disappear within twenty years.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los científicos advierten de que el glaciar podría desaparecer en veinte años.

ejemplos.frase: In a nutshell, the film is about growing up in a small town.
ejemplos.traduccion: En pocas palabras, la película trata de crecer en un pueblo.

ejemplos.frase: He attributes his success to hard work and a bit of luck.
ejemplos.traduccion: Atribuye su éxito al trabajo duro y a un poco de suerte.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Can you resume the text in 100 words?
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Can you summarise the text in 100 words?

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The author suggests to raise taxes.
The text talks about that the euro is strong.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The text argues that the euro is strong.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Talk about” takes a noun; for a statement, use a verb such as argue or state + that.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: According to the author, ... / In the author's opinion, ...

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the verb that shows the author admits a point against their view.
ejercicios.frase: The author ___ that the plan has some weaknesses, but defends it overall.
respuestas: acknowledges
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the idea from Rules and key points: the reporting verb conveys the author's attitude, and acknowledge indicates that the author admits something against their own thesis. The clue is in the structure of the sentence: the author recognises weaknesses “but defends it overall”, that is, makes a concession before defending the plan. Acknowledge that is equivalent to Spanish “reconocer que” or “admitir que”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Acknowledge” = to admit something that qualifies your own thesis.
ejercicios.traduccion: El autor reconoce que el plan tiene algunos puntos débiles, pero lo defiende en conjunto.

por_opcion.acknowledges: Correct: the author admits a point that qualifies the thesis, as “but defends it overall” confirms.
por_opcion.claims: Incorrect: claim means to state something without clear proof and does not fit a concession followed by but.
por_opcion.warns: Incorrect: warn means to tell someone about a danger; here there is no warning, but an admission.
por_opcion.dismisses: Incorrect: dismiss means to reject, the opposite of recognising weaknesses; also, it does not take that.

glosario.definicion_l: declare to be true or admit the existence or reality or truth of · report the receipt of
a flaw or weak point · powerlessness revealed by an inability to act
involving only main features · including everything

ejercicios.frase: Please resume this article in about 150 words.
respuestas: Please summarise this article in about 150 words.
Please summarize this article in about 150 words.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend mentioned in Rules and key points: resume means to start again, not to summarise. “Resumir” is summarise in British English or summarize in American English; that is why both spellings are accepted. The clue is the context: reducing an article to 150 words. “Please resume this article” would be understood as “continue reading this article”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, resume este artículo en unas 150 palabras.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please resume this article in about 150 words.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: resume means to start again.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please resumé this article in about 150 words.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Résumé is a noun (in American English, a CV); it is not the verb to summarise.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please make a resume of this article in about 150 words.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The false friend is still there; the noun is a summary and the verb is summarise.

glosario.definicion_l: short descriptive summary (of events) · a summary of your academic and work history

ejercicios.frase: The report suggests to invest more in education.
respuestas: The report suggests investing more in education.
The report suggests that we invest more in education.
The report suggests that the government invest more in education.
The report suggests that the government should invest more in education.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the grammar note from Rules and key points: suggest does not take to + infinitive. It is used with -ing (suggests investing) or with a that clause (suggests that we invest). After that, the English subjunctive (the government invest, without -s) or should + infinitive can appear; that is why all those variants are accepted. The mistake in the original sentence is a literal translation of Spanish “sugiere invertir”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El informe sugiere invertir más en educación.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The report suggests to invest more in education.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: suggest does not take to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The report suggests invest more in education.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Suggest cannot be followed by the bare infinitive; you need the gerund investing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The report suggests us to invest more in education.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Suggest does not take the structure object + to infinitive; the correct form is suggests that we invest.

glosario.definicion_l: make a proposal, declare a plan for something · drop a hint; intimate by a hint

ejercicios.frase: Economists ___ of the risk of a new housing bubble.
respuestas: warn
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes warn (that / of / against), to tell someone about a danger. The decisive clue is the preposition of after the gap and the noun risk: warn of + danger means to warn about a risk. None of the other verbs is used with of, and the content (a risk) also calls for a verb of warning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Warn of” = to warn about a danger.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los economistas advierten del riesgo de una nueva burbuja inmobiliaria.

por_opcion.warn: Correct: warn of = to warn about a danger; it fits with of and with risk.
por_opcion.claim: Incorrect: claim does not take of; it is used with that or with a direct noun (claim victory).
por_opcion.suggest: Incorrect: suggest does not take of; also, it expresses a proposal or an indication, not a warning.
por_opcion.state: Incorrect: state means to say something neutrally and takes that or a direct object, not of.

ejercicios.frase: The author attributes the decline ___ the lack of investment.
respuestas: to
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes attribute X to Y (Spanish “atribuir X a Y”). The preposition is to, like Spanish “a”, and the structure does not change: first what is being explained (the decline) and then the cause (the lack of investment). The clue is the verb attributes with its direct object already placed before the gap.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Attribute X to Y” = to say that X is caused by Y.
ejercicios.traduccion: El autor atribuye el declive a la falta de inversión.

errores_previstos.respuesta: at
errores_previstos.explicacion: Attribute does not take at; the fixed preposition is to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: for
errores_previstos.explicacion: For does not introduce the cause with attribute; the correct form is attribute X to Y.

errores_previstos.respuesta: with
errores_previstos.explicacion: With is not the preposition for attribute; the correct one is to.

glosario.definicion_l: change toward something smaller or lower · a condition inferior to an earlier condition; a gradual falling off from a better state; decline

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the verb that suggests the statement has not been proven.
ejercicios.frase: The company ___ that its product cures insomnia.
respuestas: claims
ejercicios.explicacion: According to Rules and key points, claim means to state something without clear proof and shows that the reporter keeps some distance. The clue is the context: a company that says its product cures insomnia is making a self-interested, unproven statement. By choosing claims, the person summarising shows scepticism without saying so openly.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Claim” shows some distance: it is stated, but not proven.
ejercicios.traduccion: La empresa afirma que su producto cura el insomnio.

por_opcion.claims: Correct: it states something unproven, and the verb marks distance.
por_opcion.acknowledges: Incorrect: acknowledge means to admit something against yourself; nobody “admits” that their product works.
por_opcion.concludes: Incorrect: conclude implies previous reasoning or a study, not an advertising claim.
por_opcion.outlines: Incorrect: outline means to present the main points and does not take that.

glosario.definicion_l: an assertion of a right (as to money or property) · an assertion that something is true or factual
a medicine or therapy that cures disease or relieve pain · provide a cure for, make healthy again
an inability to sleep; chronic sleeplessness

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb + particle (to demand).
ejercicios.frase: The editorial calls ___ an urgent reform of the courts.
respuestas: for
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes call for, to demand or ask for something publicly. It is a verb with a fixed preposition: without for, call means to phone or to name. The clue is the subject, an editorial, which typically demands measures, and the object, a reform. It is very common in the press: “unions call for a strike”, “the opposition calls for his resignation”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Call for” = to demand, to ask for.
ejercicios.traduccion: El editorial reclama una reforma urgente de los tribunales.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Call to” does not mean to demand; with that meaning the preposition is for.

errores_previstos.respuesta: on
errores_previstos.explicacion: Call on means to urge someone to do something (call on the government to act); here the person is missing and the object is the reform, so it takes for.

errores_previstos.respuesta: up
errores_previstos.explicacion: Call up means to phone or to summon (to the army); it does not mean to demand.

glosario.definicion_l: express the need or desire for · require as useful, just, or proper

glosario.significado: editorial (artículo de opinión de un periódico)
glosario.definicion_l: of or relating to an article stating opinions or giving perspectives · relating to or characteristic of an editor
Australian woman tennis player who won many major championships (born in 1947) · an assembly (including one or more judges) to conduct judicial business

ejercicios.frase: He ___ the criticism as politically motivated.
respuestas: dismissed
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes dismiss meaning to reject, and the example “He dismisses the idea as naive” shows the construction dismiss X as Y: to reject X because you consider it Y. The clue is the as that follows the object (“as politically motivated”). None of the other options fits that structure.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Dismiss X as Y” = to reject X because you consider it Y.
ejercicios.traduccion: Descartó las críticas por considerarlas motivadas políticamente.

por_opcion.dismissed: Correct: dismiss X as Y, to reject something because you consider it to be a certain way.
por_opcion.rejected of: Incorrect: reject takes a direct object (reject the criticism) and never takes of.
por_opcion.denied that: Incorrect: after that you would need a full clause with a verb, and here a noun follows.
por_opcion.refused: Incorrect: refuse means to say you will not do something (refuse to pay) or to turn down an offer; it is not used to reject criticism with as.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete the expression (in very few words).
ejercicios.frase: In a ___, the government's plan is too little, too late.
respuestas: nutshell
word
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes In short / In a nutshell, meaning briefly, in very few words. A nutshell is literally the shell of a nut: the idea is that everything fits into something very small. The clue is the article a after in and before the gap, which only allows nutshell. It is a fairly informal formula, useful for ending an oral summary. In a word (Spanish “en una palabra”) is also accepted; it summarises even more and is just as idiomatic.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “In a nutshell” = in very few words (also “in a word”).
ejercicios.traduccion: En pocas palabras, el plan del Gobierno es insuficiente y llega tarde.

errores_previstos.respuesta: nut
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is in a nutshell (literally, “in the shell of a nut”); in a nut does not exist.

errores_previstos.respuesta: short
errores_previstos.explicacion: “In short” has no article; with a, the expression is in a nutshell.

errores_previstos.respuesta: summary
errores_previstos.explicacion: The expression is in summary, without an article; with a, only in a nutshell.

ejercicios.enunciado: Paraphrase using the noun “decision”: start with “The”.
ejercicios.frase: The government decided to close the mine, which surprised everyone.
respuestas: The government's decision to close the mine surprised everyone.
The decision to close the mine surprised everyone.
The government's decision to close the mine took everyone by surprise.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the paraphrasing technique from Rules and key points that consists of changing the word class: the verb decided becomes the noun decision. That noun becomes the subject, and the relative clause which surprised everyone becomes the main verb. Keeping or removing the government's is accepted, as is the variant took everyone by surprise, because they all condense the idea into a noun.
ejercicios.traduccion: La decisión del Gobierno de cerrar la mina sorprendió a todos.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The government's decision of closing the mine surprised everyone.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Decision takes to + infinitive (the decision to close), not of + -ing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The decision of the government of closing the mine surprised everyone.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the Spanish structure “la decisión del Gobierno de cerrar”; in English it is the government's decision to close.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The government decided to close the mine, which surprised everyone.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the original sentence without any change: there is no nominalisation.

glosario.definicion_l: excavation in the earth from which ores and minerals are extracted · explosive device that explodes on contact; designed to destroy vehicles or ships or to kill or maim personnel

ejercicios.frase: The first chapter ___ the history of the conflict.
respuestas: outlines
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes outline / describe, to present the main points. The clue is the subject, the first chapter, and the object, the history of the conflict: an opening chapter usually presents the general framework. Outline takes a direct object, with no preposition and no that.
ejercicios.traduccion: El primer capítulo esboza la historia del conflicto.

por_opcion.outlines: Correct: it presents the main points; it fits an opening chapter and a direct object.
por_opcion.claims: Incorrect: claim introduces a debatable statement with that; you do not “claim” a history.
por_opcion.warns: Incorrect: warn means to tell someone about a danger and needs of, that or against.
por_opcion.acknowledges: Incorrect: acknowledge means to admit something against your own thesis; it does not describe what a chapter does.

glosario.definicion_l: the line that appears to bound an object · a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory
a subdivision of a written work; usually numbered and titled · any distinct period in history or in a person's life

ejercicios.frase: According to the author's opinion, the euro has been a success.
respuestas: According to the author, the euro has been a success.
In the author's opinion, the euro has been a success.
In the author's view, the euro has been a success.
ejercicios.explicacion: Rules and key points and the typical mistakes in this card point it out: according to already indicates the source of the opinion, so it is not combined with opinion. There are two solutions: according to the author or in the author's opinion / in the author's view. All three are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “According to” already indicates the source: do not add “opinion”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Según el autor, el euro ha sido un éxito.

errores_previstos.respuesta: According to the author's opinion, the euro has been a success.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: according to + opinion is redundant.

errores_previstos.respuesta: According to the author's view, the euro has been a success.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the redundancy: view is equivalent to opinion. The correct forms are according to the author or in the author's view.

errores_previstos.respuesta: According to the author's point of view, the euro has been a success.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The redundancy remains: point of view is equivalent to opinion. The correct forms are from the author's point of view or according to the author.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (to emphasise), in the present.
ejercicios.frase: The report ___ the importance of early education.
respuestas: stresses
emphasises
emphasizes
highlights
underlines
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes stress / emphasise / highlight, to give special importance to something. The clue is the object, the importance of…, which calls for a verb of emphasis, and the third-person subject (the report), which requires the -s. All five forms are accepted because they all mean to highlight and take a direct object; emphasises and emphasizes are the British and American spellings, and underlines is another valid synonym.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Stress / emphasise / highlight” = to give special importance to.
ejercicios.traduccion: El informe subraya la importancia de la educación temprana.

errores_previstos.respuesta: stress
errores_previstos.explicacion: The third-person singular -s is missing: the report stresses.

errores_previstos.respuesta: emphasises on
errores_previstos.explicacion: Emphasise takes a direct object; it does not take on (the noun does: an emphasis on).

errores_previstos.respuesta: remarks
errores_previstos.explicacion: Remark means to comment in passing and takes that or on; it does not express emphasis.

respuestas: The text deals with rural migration
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes the formula The text deals with…, the text is about. Deal with always takes the preposition with and is followed by the topic. The adjective rural goes before the noun migration, as is the rule in English. Therefore: subject (the text) + verb with preposition (deals with) + adjective + noun.
ejercicios.traduccion: El texto trata de la migración rural.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The text deals with migration rural
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies Spanish word order: the adjective goes before the noun, rural migration.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The text with deals rural migration
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition with goes after the verb: deals with.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the impersonal passive.
ejercicios.frase: People argue that the tax is unfair.
respuestas: It is argued that the tax is unfair.
The tax is argued to be unfair.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is a paraphrasing technique from Rules and key points: changing active to passive. When the subject is general (people), formal English prefers the impersonal passive It is argued that…, equivalent to Spanish “se sostiene que”: the dummy subject it takes the place of people, the verb becomes is argued and the that clause stays the same. The other, personal structure is also valid: The tax is argued to be unfair, with the subject of the subordinate clause at the front and to + infinitive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Impersonal passive: “It is argued that…” or “The tax is argued to be…”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se dice que el impuesto es injusto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It argues that the tax is unfair.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is active: it would mean that “it” argues something. You need the passive, is argued.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is argued that the tax is unfair.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The dummy subject it is missing; it is compulsory in English even though Spanish does not express it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It is argue that the tax is unfair.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The passive requires the past participle: argued.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It has been argued that the tax is unfair.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is a correct and common sentence, but it changes the tense: argue is in the present, so the passive is is argued, not has been argued.

glosario.definicion_l: not fair; marked by injustice or partiality or deception

descripcion_larga_es: Reporting verbs (argue, claim, acknowledge, warn…) and formulas for summarising and rephrasing someone else's text without copying it. They are the central tool in the summary task and in the oral presentation of an article: the chosen verb shows whether the author states, admits, warns about or demands something. They are difficult for Spanish speakers because of false friends (resume) and constructions such as suggest + -ing.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary for reporting what someone else says: reporting verbs with different nuances (state, argue, claim, acknowledge, warn, dismiss), presentation formulas (The text deals with…, According to the author…) and summarising connectors (In short, In a nutshell). It includes paraphrasing techniques such as nominalisation, synonyms and changing to the passive.
contexto.por_que_importa: A good summary does not consist of repeating “the author says” over and over: the reporting verb shows whether the author proves, suggests, admits or simply states something without proof. Choosing the wrong one changes the meaning (claim introduces distance; acknowledge, a concession) and can distort the text. In a C1-level summary task or oral presentation, this vocabulary and the ability to paraphrase are direct assessment criteria.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When summarising articles, reports or speeches, when presenting a text orally and when quoting sources in an essay. The signals are the need to attribute an idea to another person and to assess how certain it is. Spanish speakers tend to use resume for “resumir”, suggest to + infinitive and redundant combinations such as “according to the author's opinion”.
